items.title: Xi and Putin hail ties in video call as Ukraine war nears anniversary

featured_image.name: Xi, Putin hail ties in video call as Ukraine war nears anniversary

items.description:
Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin celebrated their nations' partnership during a video call on Wednesday, with both leaders signaling a commitment to deepen strategic cooperation as the fourth anniversary of Russia's invasion of Ukraine approaches later this month.

In remarks broadcast on Russian state television, Putin described the Moscow-Beijing relationship as a "stabilizing factor" amid global turbulence, while Xi called for a "grand plan" to advance bilateral ties that he said were on the "right trajectory."[1][2][3]

items.title: Oil prices rise as U.S.-Iran military incidents fuel supply fears

featured_image.name: Iranian gunboats attempted to halt US oil tanker in Strait of Hormuz

items.description:
Crude oil prices climbed on Wednesday as escalating tensions between Washington and Tehran spurred renewed concerns about supply disruptions in one of the world's most critical energy corridors. The gains followed a volatile week that saw prices swing sharply on shifting diplomatic signals and military incidents in the Persian Gulf.

Brent crude futures rose about 1% to nearly $68 per barrel, while West Texas Intermediate crude advanced approximately 1.1%. The rally built on Tuesday's gains after U.S. forces shot down an Iranian drone and armed Iranian vessels approached a U.S.-flagged tanker in the Strait of Hormuz, through which roughly 20% of the world's petroleum passes.[1][2]

items.title: QatarEnergy signs 20-year LNG deal with Malaysia's Petronas

featured_image.name: Petronas signs 20-year LNG supply deal with QatarEnergy ...

items.description:
QatarEnergy has signed a 20-year sales and purchase agreement with Petronas LNG Ltd, a subsidiary of Malaysia's state-owned Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas), to supply up to 2 million tonnes per annum of liquefied natural gas starting in 2028.[1][2][3]

The agreement marks the first long-term LNG contract between the two state energy companies and underscores Malaysia's shifting position from major exporter to prospective importer of the super-chilled fuel.[2][4]

items.title: U.S., India deepen minerals cooperation after trade deal

featured_image.name: Jaishankar holds talks with US counterpart Rubio

items.description:
External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar and U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio met in Washington on Tuesday, welcoming a trade agreement between the two nations that will slash American tariffs on Indian goods and deepen cooperation on critical minerals and energy security.

The meeting at the State Department came a day after President Donald Trump and Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced the trade deal, which reduces U.S. tariffs on Indian exports from 50% to 18%. Washington is eliminating both a 25% reciprocal tariff and a separate 25% punitive levy that had been imposed over India's purchases of Russian oil.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Gold extends rally as US-Iran tensions drive safe-haven demand

featured_image.name: Gold Prices Soared This Year. Will 2026 Bring More Record Highs?

items.description:
Gold prices surged over 2% on Wednesday, building on their strongest single-day performance since November 2008, as investors seeking refuge from escalating U.S.-Iran tensions and a weakening dollar piled into the precious metal.

Spot gold climbed 2.2% to $5,044.74 per ounce in early trading Wednesday, according to Reuters, after posting a 5.9% gain on Tuesday that marked the metal's largest daily increase in nearly two decades. The rally follows a turbulent week that saw gold swing wildly from record highs to steep losses and back again.[1][2][3]

items.title: US-UK team develops real-time Arctic sea ice prediction model

featured_image.name: Arctic sea ice drops below a grim benchmark in 2020 | Mashable

items.description:
A team of US and UK scientists has developed a new method capable of generating accurate, real-time predictions of Arctic sea ice extent, offering a crucial tool for climate monitoring and Indigenous communities who depend on stable ice conditions for their livelihoods.

The research, published in the journal Chaos by AIP Publishing on February 3, represents a breakthrough in subseasonal forecasting—predicting sea ice conditions from early summer through fall when ice coverage in the Arctic reaches its annual minimum.[1][2][3]

items.title: Trump says Putin 'kept his word' after Russia's largest 2026 attack on Ukraine

featured_image.name: Russia hammers Ukraine after halt announced by Trump, plunging thousands into frigid dark on eve of talks

items.description:
President Donald Trump defended Russian President Vladimir Putin on Tuesday after Moscow resumed devastating attacks on Ukraine's energy infrastructure, saying Putin "kept his word" on a temporary halt to strikes — despite the pause ending after four days, not the promised week.

"It was Sunday to Sunday, and he opened up and hit them hard last night," Trump told reporters in the Oval Office. "He kept his word on that. One week is a lot — we'll take anything, because it's really cold over there."[1][2]

The comments came hours after Russia launched what Ukrainian officials described as the largest attack of 2026, deploying more than 450 drones and 70 missiles at energy infrastructure during temperatures below -20°C (-4°F). The assault left over 1,000 residential buildings in Kyiv without heating and caused severe damage to power facilities in Kharkiv.[3][4][5]

items.title: CK Hutchison launches arbitration against Panama over port ruling

featured_image.name: CK Hutchison faces limited legal options after Panama voids port rights: experts

items.description:
CK Hutchison Holdings announced Wednesday that its Panama Ports Company unit has initiated international arbitration proceedings against the Republic of Panama, following a court ruling last week that annulled its licenses to operate two major ports along the Panama Canal.

Panama's Supreme Court ruled on January 29 that the contracts were unconstitutional, citing exclusive privileges and tax exemptions granted to the Hong Kong-based conglomerate. The decision threatens CK Hutchison's planned $23 billion sale of its global port operations to a consortium led by BlackRock and Mediterranean Shipping Company.

items.title: Starmer, Trump agree to work together on Diego Garcia base

featured_image.name: Starmer, Trump Discuss UK Base Deal Panned by White House ...

items.description:
Prime Minister Keir Starmer and President Donald Trump held discussions on Tuesday regarding the future of the joint UK-US military base on Diego Garcia, marking their first known conversation on the topic since Trump branded the sovereignty deal an "act of great stupidity" last month.

According to Downing Street, the two leaders "recognised its strategic importance" and "agreed their governments would continue working closely to guarantee the future operation of the base and speak again soon."[1][2][3]

items.title: UAE and Colossal Biosciences to build genetic 'Noah's Ark' in Dubai

featured_image.name: Dallas-Based Colossal Gets $60M From U.A.E., Will Build a ...

items.description:
The United Arab Emirates and Colossal Biosciences announced a $60 million partnership on Tuesday to create the world's first BioVault, a genetic preservation facility that company leaders describe as a "modern-day Noah's Ark" designed to safeguard endangered species from extinction.

The initiative, unveiled at the World Governments Summit in Dubai, will establish the Colossal BioVault and World Preservation Lab as a permanent feature at Dubai's Museum of the Future, with construction expected to be completed by 2027. The announcement marks one of the largest conservation biotechnology deals between a government and a private company.[1][2]

items.title: Starmer, Trump discuss Ukraine as peace talks resume

featured_image.name: UK's Starmer discussed 'tough and fair' Ukraine peace deal with ...

items.description:
British Prime Minister Keir Starmer spoke with U.S. President Donald Trump on Tuesday about the deteriorating situation in Ukraine, where overnight Russian strikes left thousands without heat amid freezing temperatures, according to the UK government. The conversation came as Ukrainian negotiators traveled to Abu Dhabi for a second round of trilateral peace discussions scheduled for Wednesday and Thursday.[1][2][3]

Russia launched 450 drones and over 60 missiles overnight on February 2-3, targeting energy infrastructure across eight Ukrainian regions, according to Ukraine's Foreign Affairs Minister Andrii Sybiha. The attacks knocked out heating for 1,170 residential buildings in Kyiv as temperatures dropped to -17 Celsius (1.4 Fahrenheit), Mayor Vitali Klitschko reported. The strikes also hit thermal power plants in Kharkiv and Dnipro, leaving at least four people injured.[4]

The assault marked the heaviest attack on Ukraine's energy sector in 2026 and signaled the end of a brief ceasefire on energy targets. Trump had announced on January 29 that Russian President Vladimir Putin agreed to pause strikes on energy facilities for a week, but the Kremlin said the pause would only last until February 1.[5][6][7]

items.title: Nvidia CEO says OpenAI deal on track, dismisses drama

featured_image.name: Nvidia's Jensen Huang denies OpenAI deal rumors: 'There's no drama'

items.description:
Nvidia Corp. CEO Jensen Huang said the chipmaker still expects to put money into OpenAI, pushing back on reports that a headline-grabbing plan floated last year had stalled and emphasizing that any investment would unfold in steps rather than as a single, immediate $100 billion check.[1][2][3]

In an interview with CNBC, Huang said Nvidia would participate in OpenAI’s next fundraising round and would also be open to investing in an eventual initial public offering, calling the relationship “on track” and dismissing the notion of internal “drama.”[2][3][1]

items.title: Markets tumble on AI disruption fears and Bitcoin drops

featured_image.name: Wall Street ends sharply down as traders fret about AI disruption

items.description:
Global equities slid Tuesday as a new wave of investor anxiety hit technology and data-heavy stocks, with concerns that fast-improving “agentic” AI tools could pressure margins and upend business models. Bitcoin also sank to its lowest level since November 2024, adding to a broader “risk-off” tone across markets.[1][2][3][4][5]

The selloff was catalyzed by fresh attention on AI moving from back-end capabilities into workflow products—most notably a legal-focused tool from Anthropic—prompting investors to reassess which software and information businesses are defensible as automation improves.[2][5][6]

items.title: US Navy shoots down Iranian drone approaching carrier

featured_image.name: US military says it shot down an Iranian drone in Arabian Sea

items.description:
A US F-35C fighter jet shot down an Iranian drone that "aggressively approached" the aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln in the Arabian Sea on Tuesday, marking a direct military encounter between American and Iranian forces just days before high-stakes diplomatic talks are set to begin.

The incident occurred as the Lincoln was transiting approximately 500 miles from Iran's southern coast when an Iranian Shahed-139 drone "unnecessarily maneuvered toward the ship," according to US Central Command spokesman Capt. Tim Hawkins. The drone continued its approach "despite de-escalatory measures taken by US forces operating in international waters," prompting the F-35C to intercept and destroy it in self-defense.[1][2][3][4]

No American service members were injured and no US equipment was damaged during the encounter.[5][6]

items.title: China warns Panama of 'heavy price' after canal port ruling

featured_image.name: China calls Panama court ruling on CK Hutchison port contracts 'shameful, pathetic'

items.description:
China on Tuesday denounced a Panamanian Supreme Court ruling that struck down the legal basis for a Hong Kong company’s long-running concessions to operate two ports at either end of the Panama Canal, escalating a dispute that has become entangled in U.S.-China rivalry and a major global ports transaction.[1][2][3]

In a statement carried by China’s Hong Kong and Macau Affairs Office, Beijing described the decision as “absurd,” “shameful and pathetic,” and warned Panama it could face “heavy” political and economic consequences if it pressed ahead—language that signals the case has moved beyond a commercial disagreement into a diplomatic flashpoint.[4][2][3]

items.title: US-backed consortium agrees to buy 40% of Glencore's Congo mines

featured_image.name: Glencore plans to sell 40% stake in Congo mines to US-backed ...

items.description:
Glencore PLC said it has signed a **non-binding memorandum of understanding** that could see a US-backed investment group acquire **40% of Glencore’s interests** in two major copper-and-cobalt operations in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC): Mutanda Mining (Mumi) and Kamoto Copper Company (KCC). The companies said the talks imply a **combined enterprise value of about $9 billion** for the two assets.[1][2][3]

The prospective buyer is the **Orion Critical Mineral Consortium (Orion CMC)**, which Glencore said was established in October 2025 and is led by Orion Resource Partners in partnership with the US government. Glencore shares rose in London trading after the announcement.[4][3]

items.title: EU and UK hold London talks on trade, defense cooperation

featured_image.name: UK and EU reset relations with landmark deals at London summit

items.description:
European Union and UK officials opened a fresh push for closer cooperation this week, using meetings in London to accelerate negotiations on easing post-Brexit trade frictions and rebuilding security ties as the 10th anniversary of the 2016 referendum approaches.[1][2][3]

The discussions brought together UK Chancellor Rachel Reeves and senior EU figures including Maroš Šefčovič and Valdis Dombrovskis, amid growing agreement on both sides that the current geopolitical and trade environment is pushing Europe and Britain toward more structured collaboration.[2][3][1]

items.title: Apple brings AI agents from Anthropic, OpenAI to Xcode

featured_image.name: Xcode 26.3 unlocks the power of agentic coding - Apple

items.description:
Apple on Tuesday announced the release of Xcode 26.3, bringing agentic AI coding capabilities to its flagship development environment through integrations with Anthropic's Claude Agent and OpenAI's Codex. The update allows AI models to autonomously explore projects, write code, run tests, and fix errors within the IDE used by developers building apps for iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Apple Watch.

The Xcode 26.3 Release Candidate is available to all Apple Developer Program members today, with a broader App Store release expected soon.[1][2]

items.title: US shoots down Iranian drone approaching aircraft carrier

featured_image.name: US military shoots down Iranian drone approaching USS Abraham Lincoln in  Arabian Sea, official says

items.description:
A US F-35C fighter jet shot down an Iranian drone that "aggressively approached" the USS Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier in the Arabian Sea on Tuesday, marking a sharp escalation in maritime tensions between Washington and Tehran just days before planned nuclear negotiations.

The Shahed-139 drone was destroyed as the carrier sailed approximately 500 miles from Iran's southern coast, according to U.S. Central Command. No American personnel were harmed and no equipment was damaged.[1][2][3]

items.title: Poll: 76% of Greenlanders oppose joining the United States

featured_image.name: US voters widely opposed to taking Greenland by military force

items.description:
A new poll has found that 76% of Greenlanders oppose the idea of their Arctic territory becoming part of the United States, with widespread concerns about trading their Danish welfare system for American healthcare, senior care, and education systems.

The survey, conducted by Danish pollster Sune Steffen Hansen in January 2026, reveals that just 8% of Greenland's residents believe it would be advantageous to join the United States, while 16% remain undecided. According to a separate report in The Wall Street Journal, only 3% of Greenlanders view the benefits provided by the U.S. government as "very positive," while a substantial 59% have a predominantly or strongly negative perception.[1][2]
